text:
elyse: quick sync — running into weird cancellation/timeouts across clients. when a user aborts a streaming response right as the SDK refreshes auth, we sometimes retry the request and the server sees two connections. anyone else?

samir: yup saw this in node and python. often the retry-layer doesn't check the abort signal after auth refresh. result: request starts again.

vinh: in rust client i noticed the cancellation token is dropped but the auth future still completes and triggers request::retry(). we need clearer ownership of the cancel path.

kate: repro steps? i can try locally.

elyse: minimal repro — start a streaming chat, call AbortController.abort() immediately after first chunk, force token refresh (set exp < now). node logs show: 
```
[info] starting stream request
[info] token expired -> refresh
[info] client abort received
[info] retrying request after auth
```
server sees two open streams for same session id.

samir: interesting. node behavior likely from our fetch wrapper: auth middleware awaits token then calls downstream without re-checking signal. in fetch, passing `signal` to the new Request is necessary.

dima: python's requests-based streaming will also re-open if our retry decorator wraps the whole call. we added a short-circuit check post-refresh but it's flaky with streaming iterators.

vinh: rust solution idea: make auth refresh return a Result<Token,Canceled>. after refresh, return early if canceled. also make retry logic consult the same CancellationTokenRegister.

kate: for node i can do `if (signal.aborted) throw new AbortError()` right after token refresh before issuing fetch. cheap fix but we should codify it.

elyse: agreed — let's standardize: 1) auth refresh must acknowledge abort (check signal after await). 2) retry decisions must call `isCanceled()` before re-issuing. 3) streaming helpers should surface an early-close so iterator stops and we don't start retries.

samir: also watch for edge: if retry policy has backoff, we might re-schedule after abort; so check at schedule time as well.

dima: can we make a small cross-SDK compatibility test? something like: spawn stream, trigger instant abort, expire token mid-flow, assert server got only 1 connection.

elyse: yes — create a harness that simulates token exp and counts conns. i'll draft the test harness and add to sdk-interop repo.

vinh: should we update our SDK contracts doc? i can add a short section: "Cancellation semantics and auth" with examples for Node/Py/Rust/Go.

elyse: please do. owners: kate for node patch (PR request incoming), dima for python, vinh for rust doc + change, samir to help verify node/pys server logs. i'll open issues/PRs and tag folks.

ci-bot: created issue #1243 in sdk-interop: "cross-sdk: cancel/auth race causing duplicate streams" (link: https://git.internal/sdks/issues/1243)

kate: grabbing it now, will push a small fix + unit test. can we aim for T-3?

samir: i'm around today for quick reviews. ping me in thread.

elyse: thanks all. follow-ups: kate -> node PR, dima -> py test, vinh -> doc + rust check, samir -> validation. i'll post the harness link here once done. :thumbsup:
